title: Anticipatory Scheduling of the Minimum Magnetising-Current Limit in MTPA-Controlled Induction Motor Drives for Electric Vehicles
content: In electric-vehicle induction-motor drives, maximum-torque-per-ampere (MTPA) control improves partial-load efficiency by reducing rotor flux, but the resulting remagnetisation delay can impair torque delivery at traction onset. Fixed minimum magnetising-current limits improve response but impose losses throughout the drive cycle. This paper schedules the limit with a closed-form rule derived from rotor-flux dynamics and a binary warning from brake-pedal release at low speed, without predicting future torque or modifying the MTPA controller. In two simulated urban cycles, the rule alone, reacting to the present demand, eliminates the onsets degraded under the nominal limit at no energy cost, and the warning cuts the remaining peak torque error about threefold for under 1.5 Wh. On the New York City Cycle, relative to the lowest-energy fixed limit without degraded onsets, the supervisor with warning reduces peak torque error from 19.36 to 5.16 N·m and energy from 132.57 to 129.34 Wh. Warning leads of about one rotor time constant, as provided by brake release, also make peak torque error far less sensitive to rotor-resistance variation. Experiments on an 18.5 kW drive confirm real-time anticipative magnetisation: mean estimated onset flux reaches 0.81 Wb, with stator copper loss only 1.27 Wh above the nominal limit.
